fact_check.claim: Eight landlords owned about $153 million of Collegetown property
fact_check.note: Source gives about $153 million for eight landlords (2013).

fact_check.claim: Those eight owned 4,013 of an estimated 6,110 bedrooms, almost two-thirds
fact_check.note: 4,013 of an estimated 6,110 bedrooms; 4,013/6,110 is about 66%.

fact_check.claim: The first two owners each held more than $38 million of property
fact_check.note: Source says Novarr and Jason Fane each own more than $38 million.

fact_check.claim: John Novarr held 1,559 of the beds, largely through the Collegetown Terrace project
fact_check.note: Source says the 1,559 beds are owned by Novarr, 'whose mammoth Collegetown Terrace project has significantly expanded the stock'. It does not say the 1,559 beds come largely through Terrace.

fact_check.claim: Owners named: Jason Fane; Avramis, Lambrou and Lower families; Travis Hyde, Pam Johnston, Matoula Halkiopoulus
fact_check.note: All names appear in the source.

fact_check.claim: The Sun noted the numbers do not prove the market was consolidating further
fact_check.note: Source says the numbers 'do not prove that Collegetown real estate has become increasingly consolidated in the hands of a few landowners'.

fact_check.claim: 2004 Sun feature: one line about a management company is a single tenant's suspicion about deposits
fact_check.note: The deposit line is from Jeff Hull of Ithaca Renting Company, who says 'most would say' the company is trying to rip off their security deposit. It is a manager relaying a general perception, not a single tenant's suspicion. The article is interview-based and names landlords, and its themes (repairs, lost rent checks, deposits, intrusion) are as described. The page shows no date; the URL says 2004-12-02.

fact_check.claim: Niko Nguyen 2022 column argues a small group controls Collegetown; describes his apartment problems and a friend's mold and burst pipe
fact_check.note: Supported: 'managed by only a handful of landlords', North Quarry apartment problems, friend's mold and burst pipe, early-leasing rush.

fact_check.claim: Certificate of compliance: owner must apply and schedule inspection before the current certificate expires
fact_check.note: Page says to do so 'prior to the expiration date of the current Certificate of Compliance'.

fact_check.claim: A multiple dwelling (three or more units, or a unit with six or more unrelated people) can hold a valid certificate for three years
fact_check.note: Source gives 3 years for multiple dwellings, defined as 3+ units or 6+ unrelated persons.

fact_check.claim: Building Division 607-274-6508, 8 AM to 4 PM Monday through Friday
fact_check.note: Phone and hours match.

fact_check.claim: The city page does not describe a public lookup
fact_check.note: Page mentions no public lookup.

fact_check.claim: Cornell and the Building Division built an online tool showing fire safety, alarms, egress and construction type for City of Ithaca rentals, updated daily; properties outside the city are exempt
fact_check.note: Source: joint tool, shows 'fire safety, notifications systems, emergency egresses, construction type and property use', data updated daily, outside-city properties exempt. Egress is not yet part of the safety score; the article does not say it is scored.

fact_check.claim: Cornell's off-campus resources page lists Building Division 607-274-6508, CDRC 607-273-9347, LAWNY Ithaca 607-273-3667, Cornell Law Tenant Advocacy Practicum 607-301-1560, and the Ithaca Tenants' Union
fact_check.note: All four numbers match; ITU is listed with a website and a landlord issue form.

fact_check.claim: Search the Ithaca Tenants' Union for tenant reports on an address or owner
fact_check.note: Site loads, but the home page shows no tenant reports or landlord lookup, only a tenant rights guide, a Get Help page and similar links. Cornell's page says ITU has a landlord issue form, not a searchable report list.

fact_check.claim: Sun 2018 report on 117 Thurston Avenue
fact_check.note: The article text says '117 Thurston' only; 'Avenue' could not be confirmed from the text.

fact_check.claim: Certificate of compliance at 117 Thurston expired in November 2015; students learned after signing
fact_check.note: Building Department email says it expired Nov. 18, 2015.

fact_check.claim: Repeated toilet overflows, about three days without hot water, city inspection found insufficient heat
fact_check.note: Overflows about every five days from early August; about three days without hot water from Aug. 20; Oct. 29 inspection found heat insufficient.

fact_check.claim: Landlord called the certificate 'good to have' but not required; code enforcement director said certificates are required for all dwellings; one student slept in a library; unclear whether the Building Department could do more than warnings
fact_check.note: All match. Barbara Lower said 'good to have' but 'not required'; Mike Niechwiadowicz said required for all dwellings.

fact_check.claim: Under NY GOL 7-108 a landlord must return the deposit with an itemized statement within 14 days after move-out, and forfeits the right to keep any of it if they miss that window
fact_check.note: Subdivision 1-a(e) says 14 days and forfeiture. The scope of 1-a is narrower than the article implies; see the next entry.

fact_check.claim: A deposit may not exceed one month's rent 'in the settings it covers'
fact_check.note: 1-a(a) says no deposit shall exceed one month's rent, but the text as retrieved limits subdivision 1-a to listed categories and excludes rent-regulated units. The article does not say which tenants are covered, so a student cannot tell whether the 14-day rule and the cap apply to a Collegetown lease. The writer must read the subdivision text and state its coverage precisely.

fact_check.claim: A city amendment effective May 31, 2022 requires landlords to give current tenants at least 120 days' written notice before renewing, showing the unit or signing a new tenant; waivable only with language on the lease's first page
fact_check.note: The source is an opinion column by the sponsoring council member (Chapter 258-10(A), passed April 6, 'takes effect May 31'). It supports the figures, but this is a legal rule resting on a newspaper column, not the ordinance. It needs an official source (City of Ithaca Code 258-10(A) or a city page).

fact_check.claim: No official list of bad Collegetown landlords exists; Cornell's resources page points to the Building Division and tenant groups
fact_check.note: The page lists no ranking of landlords; it lists agencies and the ITU.

beats_top.query: ithaca landlords to avoid collegetown reviews
beats_top.why: The #1 result is a 2002 Sun piece about one unsafe building. It names no current landlord and offers only the advice to ask about a certificate of compliance. Our page gives that check plus the ownership data, deposit and renewal rules, and contacts. It stops short of the specific record lookup a student wants.
changes: Link the Cornell safety-rating tool itself (not just the explainer page) and say it also recognizes landlords who exceed compliance requirements, if the Cornell page states that; the search result suggests it does. This is the nearest thing to a current landlord check.
Add a short 'if you only have 10 minutes' checklist near the top: the Building Division call, the Cornell tool, and the three deposit and renewal clauses.
Be exact about who the deposit rules cover, so the student knows whether they apply to their lease.

fixes: Change the Novarr bullet to match the source: 'John Novarr, who owned 1,559 of the beds; his Collegetown Terrace project had significantly expanded the student housing stock' (https://cornellsun.com/2013/05/02/collegetown-housing-market-scrutinized/). Do not say the beds came largely through Collegetown Terrace.

Change the 2004 feature description: the deposit line is Jeff Hull of Ithaca Renting Company saying 'most would say' the company is trying to rip off their security deposit. It is a manager relaying a general perception, which the article does not verify. Remove 'a single tenant's suspicion'.

Replace the Sun opinion column as the source for the 120-day notice rule with the ordinance or an official city page (City of Ithaca Code Chapter 258-10(A), https://ecode360.com/ or a cityofithacany.gov page). Keep the Sun column only as context. State the effective date and the first-page waiver language from the official text. If no official page can be found, say the rule is described by its council sponsor in a Sun column and tell students to confirm with the Building Division.

In the deposit bullet, read the full text of https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GOB/7-108 and state who subdivision 1-a covers, and say whether it covers an ordinary Collegetown lease. If coverage is not clear from the statute, drop the one-month cap sentence and the 'in the settings it covers' hedge, and tell students to confirm with Legal Assistance of Western New York (607-273-3667).

In step 5 and the Ithaca Tenants' Union mentions, do not say tenant reports can be searched there. Say the ITU has a tenant rights guide and a landlord issue form (https://ithacatu.org) and that reports are not published as a searchable list.
Change 'Sun's 2018 report on 117 Thurston Avenue' to '117 Thurston' (the article gives no street type).
